ZhijianL.OutlineShortcutsTip:
Outline shortcuts
Arrow keys: switch selected node
Enter: add sibling (center topic: add child)
Tab: demote under previous sibling
Shift+Tab: promote to parent level
Alt+Up/Down: move among siblings
ZhijianL.MindMapShortcutsTip:
Mind map shortcuts
Arrow keys: switch selected topic
Enter: add sibling (center topic: add child)
Tab / Shift+Tab: add child
Alt+Up/Down: move among siblings
Delete: delete selected topic
ZhijianL.AboutDescription: A local-first, Markdown-first mind map editor built with Avalonia / AtomUI.

ZhijianL.ProductPlanTemplateDescription: Useful for mapping users, goals, features, experience, and release plans.
ZhijianL.ProductPlanTemplateMarkdown:
# Product Brief
Turn a product idea into a reviewable, buildable, and testable brief. Fill the notes first, then adjust the mind-map structure.
## Users and Scenarios
Start with who this serves and where the need appears before listing features.
### Target Users
Name the primary user, decision maker, and usage frequency. Example: content creators who plan 3-5 topics each week.
### Core Pain Points
Use the user's language. Add frequency, impact, and current workarounds.
### Key Jobs
List the real jobs users want done, not system menu names. Each job should lead to a clear outcome.
## Goals and Metrics
Translate product value into observable metrics so the release can be judged later.
### Product Goals
Describe the main experience this version should improve, such as reducing time to first usable mind map.
### Success Metrics
Include behavior and quality metrics, such as template usage, save rate, export success rate, and feedback quality.
### Non-goals
Write the boundaries explicitly to prevent scope creep, especially advanced features or long-tail formats.
## Core Features
Break user jobs into the smallest useful loop and protect the main path first.
### Capture and Creation
Explain where users start: blank document, template, imported file, or pasted Markdown.
### Editing and Organization
Prioritize frequent editing actions such as adding nodes, drag/drop, notes, undo, and redo.
### Import and Export
Separate editable saving from one-off export so users understand format support.
## Interaction and Experience
Design for continuous editing so users do not keep leaving the canvas.
### Onboarding
Record the three things first-time users must learn instead of turning help into a manual copy.
### Fast Actions
List actions that deserve visible controls and expert actions that can live in shortcuts.
### Error States
Cover blank, loading, parse failure, unsaved close, missing file, and similar states.
## Release Plan
Bring the brief down to scope, acceptance, and risks so product, engineering, and QA align.
### Version Scope
State what this release includes and what moves to later versions.
### Acceptance Criteria
Describe user-completable outcomes, such as creating a mind map from a template and saving it as Markdown.
### Risks and Dependencies
Track technical risks, platform limits, third-party dependencies, and items needing confirmation.
ZhijianL.MeetingNotesTemplateDescription: Useful for agendas, decisions, action items, and follow-up risks.
ZhijianL.MeetingNotesTemplateMarkdown:
# Meeting Notes
Turn discussion into decisions, action items, and follow-up risks for easy sharing after the meeting.
## Meeting Goal
Write the one problem this meeting must solve. A clear goal keeps the notes focused.
## Agenda
Prepare topics before the meeting, then add background, disagreements, and outcomes during the meeting.
### Topic One
Capture the background, current blocker, and who needs to decide.
### Topic Two
Capture options, tradeoffs, and decision criteria.
## Key Decisions
Only write confirmed decisions here. Put unresolved items under risks and open questions.
## Action Items
Each action should include task, owner, due date, and the result that proves it is done.
### Owner
Use one accountable owner. Collaborators can be mentioned in the note.
### Due Date
Use a concrete date or before next sync instead of as soon as possible.
## Risks and Open Questions
Track dependencies, missing information, and disagreements that may affect progress.
## Next Meeting
Write the next sync time, purpose, and materials to prepare.
ZhijianL.StudyNotesTemplateDescription: Useful for capturing concepts, sources, questions, examples, and reflection.
ZhijianL.StudyNotesTemplateMarkdown:
# Study Notes
Turn source material into your own knowledge structure instead of copying text. Add one sentence of personal understanding to each node.
## Core Concepts
Define the most important concepts first, then note how they differ from nearby ideas.
## Sources
Record source, credibility, and applicable context so future-you can judge whether it still applies.
### Articles
Add title, author, link, or keywords, plus the most valuable section.
### Videos
Capture timestamps and key points so you do not need to rewatch from the beginning.
### Books
Record chapter, page, and a short summary for long-term reference.
## Questions
Keep unresolved questions here and revisit them first during review.
## Examples and Practice
Connect concepts to real examples, ideally with a small exercise you can reproduce.
## Reflection
Fill this after studying, not at the beginning.
### What I Understand
Explain the idea in your own words. If you can teach it, you probably understand it.
### What to Learn Next
Record weak spots, next sources, and when you plan to practice.

ZhijianL.TourWelcomeDescription: This tour highlights the real file entry, outline editor, Markdown switch, mind-map canvas, and bottom navigation.
ZhijianL.TourFilesDescription: Create, open editable files, import, open folders, save, export, and reach recent files here. After opening a folder, the Files tab lists supported files.
ZhijianL.TourOutlineDescription: The Outline tab is the main input area. Press Enter for siblings, Tab or Shift+Tab for hierarchy, or drag the dot to reposition nodes.
ZhijianL.TourToggleDescription: This button switches to Markdown. Markdown stays synchronized with the outline and mind map for text-first editing.
ZhijianL.TourMindMapDescription: Mind-map nodes support inline titles and notes, right-click menus, floating tools, and drag/drop hierarchy changes. The control also includes basic node operations.
ZhijianL.TourCanvasDescription: Pinch with two fingers on a touchpad to zoom; two-finger scroll or the mouse wheel pans. Ctrl/⌘ + wheel also zooms at the pointer, and dragging the center topic, Space+left drag, or middle drag pans.
ZhijianL.TourStatusDescription: Undo, redo, left-pane visibility, mini map, center root, zoom, and mind-map shortcuts live here. The Help menu reopens this guide at any time.
